title: TOLAP Security Context (canonical signing projection)
description: The envelope a TOLAP security context projects into before signing, as specified normatively by docs/canonical-enforcement-spec.md sections 1 and 2. This describes the SIGNED SHAPE ONLY -- not any SDK's native context type, and NOT the artifact a server puts on the wire. Validate a canonical payload against this schema; validating a transported artifact against it will fail, correctly. The three SDKs deliberately keep different public models (.NET carries a policies array, Python and TypeScript a single effective policy) and converge only at this form, which is why the projection rather than any model is what has a schema. Fields a wire artifact carries and this schema therefore excludes: `signature`, `algorithm` and `integrity` (a signature cannot cover itself), `resolvedAt` (the TypeScript spelling of `issuedAt`), `effectivePolicy` (the single-policy spelling of `policies`), and `kid` (a key hint that sits outside the signed bytes precisely so it cannot change them -- see docs/policy-server.md on rotation). `additionalProperties` is false because the signed bytes are exhaustively specified: an unrecognized key in a canonical payload is either an unsigned field someone believed was signed, or a signed one the other SDKs do not produce. Optional properties are OMITTED entirely when absent rather than emitted as null, which is what makes each of them a backward-compatible addition -- see section 2 rule 6.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for validation tooling.

version.description: TOLAP schema version. Inside the signed payload, so it cannot be rewritten.

userId.description: The principal this context was issued for.

issuedAt.description: When the context was issued. UTC with a 'Z' suffix, truncated to millisecond precision (section 2 rule 5).

expiresAt.description: When the context expires. Inside the signed payload, so an expiry cannot be extended without the key. A missing or unparseable value is rejected rather than treated as 'never expires'.

policies.description: The effective policy, with its integrity block stripped. Validate each entry against effective-policy.schema.json in FRAGMENT mode -- a signed payload necessarily omits `integrity`, since a signature cannot cover itself. Deliberately not a cross-file $ref: no schema in this directory uses one (effective-policy duplicates maskingRule rather than referencing policy-definition's), because the four validators in this repository -- Python's jsonschema, the server's Ajv, and the two native SDK readers -- would each need a resolver configured with a local store, and one of them silently not having it would mean a schema that validates nothing. Section 14 handles the resulting duplication with equality tests instead. An array because that is the wire shape section 2 rule 3 mandates, but a context governs exactly one data source: every enforcement path reads only the first element, so a context carrying two would sign both and enforce one, and all three SDKs refuse that. An EMPTY array is valid -- it grants nothing, which is safe -- whereas two is the ambiguity worth refusing.

jti.description: Unique context identifier for replay detection (section 13.1). Signed when present, so a replay guard cannot be defeated by stripping it. An empty string normalizes to absent, so '' and omitted cannot yield two different signatures -- hence minLength 1: an empty value must never appear in a canonical payload.

declaredPurpose.description: The purpose this context was resolved for (section 15.1). Matched against a policy's purposeProfile.purposeId exactly and case-sensitively. Signed when present, so a purpose-scoped context cannot be repurposed by swapping it or stripping it. Empty normalizes to absent. Records the purpose the caller ASSERTED; TOLAP checks that assertion against the policy set, not the caller's honesty about it (section 13).

delegationChain.description: How authority reached the principal making the call, oldest hop first (section 15.3). Signed hop for hop: appending, mutating, reordering or removing a hop invalidates the signature, which is the precondition for validating the chain at all -- an unsigned chain can be rewritten by the principal it constrains. An EMPTY chain normalizes to absent, hence minItems 1: it carries no hops and so asserts nothing. Note this is the opposite of the null-versus-empty rule for allow-lists (section 3), because that rule concerns restrictions and this concerns claims.

delegationHop.description: One hop in a delegation chain. Each hop may hold less authority than its parent and never more.

principalId.description: Identifier of the principal at this hop.

principalType.description: Kind of principal. user: a human, only ever the first hop. agent: an autonomous agent acting on a principal's behalf. service: a non-agent component such as an orchestrator passing work along. A closed set, so an unrecognized value is refused at deserialization rather than reaching chain validation as a value no narrowing rule covers.

declaredPurpose.description: The purpose in force at this hop. May be a glob, so a parent can delegate a family of purposes ('campaign-*'); this is why the pattern is looser than the envelope's declaredPurpose, which is a concrete assertion rather than a delegable scope. A child purpose must equal its parent, be matched by its parent glob, or extend it on a '-' segment boundary -- a plain prefix test would let 'campaign-x' authorize 'campaign-xyz-evil'. Comparison is case-sensitive. Absent on either side of a comparison adds no constraint.

delegatedAt.description: When the hop was created. Part of the signed bytes, so it is truncated to millisecond precision like every other timestamp (section 2 rule 5) -- the three runtimes do not agree below that. Recorded for the audit trail; narrowing does not consider it.

scopeNarrowing.description: The scopes still IN FORCE at this hop -- not the scopes this hop removed. Each hop's set must be a subset of its parent's, so an empty set leaves nothing for a child to claim (section 3). Named for its effect rather than its contents, which is the reading the subset rule requires. Absent on either side adds no constraint.
